title: Lifecycle correlation does not yet cover every worker/tool event
summary: The real worker lifecycle skeleton is correlated end-to-end locally, but detailed OpenCode read/write/step events and some model-detail events reconstructed from secondary logs can still have correlation=null.
claims: TERM→OC→QWEN→LLAMA lifecycle events share one correlation_id.
Detailed OpenCode read/write/step-finish and some QWEN diagnostic events can remain uncorrelated.
Inbound MCP/ChatGPT work still has source_quality=unknown or declared rather than transport-observed turn/message identity.
decision: Keep OBS-04 and GW-01 open; next causal-provenance work must propagate correlation into all child events and allocate it before inbound MCP/tool dispatch.
rationale: A lifecycle skeleton alone is insufficient for end-to-end trace reconstruction or turn-level source navigation.

evidence.note: Explicitly records correlated lifecycle and uncorrelated detailed events.
OC/QWEN detail rows were visible without inherited correlation while terminal lifecycle rows were correlated.
